claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

Thank you for waiting. Now I can help assess your eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 3 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old and lives with you.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I've recently moved here actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances.

**What is your immigration or residence status in the UK?** For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another type of visa or residence status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about all the technical terms to be honest. I've moved here recently but I don't know exactly what my right-to-reside position is called or how it works.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly understandable - the terminology can be confusing. Let me ask some simpler questions to help clarify your situation.

**Where did you move to the UK from?** For example, were you living in another European country, or elsewhere in the world?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those details right now. I'm just trying to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for Alex. Is there a way to check my eligibility without going through all of this?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you'd prefer not to go into those details, and I appreciate your patience with the questions.

Unfortunately, residence status is a key part of Child Benefit eligibility rules. According to the official guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK - but there are specific rules about having the "right to reside" in the UK, particularly for those who have recently moved here.

Without understanding your residence status, I cannot accurately determine whether you would be eligible for Child Benefit or not.

However, since you do have a 3-year-old child (Alex) living with you in the UK, and you are responsible for him, let me ask one more basic question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

Based on what you've told me:
- You have Alex, who is 3 years old
- Alex lives with you
- You're responsible for him
- You live in the UK
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

These are positive factors. However, because you've recently moved to the UK and you're unable to provide information about your residence status or right to reside, I cannot make a definitive assessment of your eligibility.

The right to reside in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility, and the rules vary significantly depending on factors like:
- Your nationality
- Your immigration status
- Whether you're working or have other circumstances that give you the right to reside

**Is there anything else about your situation that you can share that might help assess your eligibility?** For example, are you working in the UK, or do you have any documentation about your right to live here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Look, I understand it's important, but I genuinely don't know the answer to these questions about my right to reside. I haven't sorted all that out yet - I've just been focused on settling Alex in and getting things organized. 

Is there someone I can speak to who can help me figure out my residence status first, or can I just apply and they'll sort it out?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - moving to a new country with a young child is a lot to manage, and these administrative matters can be overwhelming.

You're right that figuring out your residence status is an important first step. Here's what I'd suggest:

**You can contact the Child Benefit Office directly**, and they can help assess your specific situation and guide you through what documentation you might need. They deal with these questions regularly and can give you personalized advice based on your circumstances.

You could also apply for Child Benefit, and HMRC will assess your eligibility as part of processing your application - they'll ask for the necessary documentation and information they need to make a decision.

Given what you've shared with me:
- Alex is 3 years old and lives with you
- You're responsible for him
- You live in the UK
- Nobody else is claiming for him

These factors suggest you could potentially be eligible, **but** because you don't currently have information about your right to reside in the UK (which is a fundamental eligibility requirement), I cannot definitively determine whether you are eligible or not.

Let me now provide my assessment based on our conversation.
